newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin okays Chechnya plan except early pullout.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin okays Chechnya plan except early pullout.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Thursday he had backed the peace deal for Chechnya signed by his envoy Alexander Lebed except for the part providing for an early withdrawal of Russian troops from the rebel region.

"I support his action, and I have backed the latest plan of action with the exception of one issue -- the fast and prompt withdrawal of troops -- I think we should not be in a hurry to do that. The rest I have backed and fully approved," Yeltsin said in a television interview.
It was the first direct comment Yeltsin had made on the plan, signed at the weekend by his security adviser Lebed and Chechen rebel chief-of-staff Aslan Maskhadov.
The plan includes a compromise on the issue at the heart of the conflict -- the future political status of Chechnya -- by putting off a decision for five years.

It also provides for the withdrawal of most of the troops sent to Chechnya by Yeltsin in December 1994 to crush the rebels, and for the establishment of Russian-rebel patrols to take the place of the troops and their separatist opponents in the capital Grozny.

Yeltsin did not make clear how long he wanted his forces to stay in the North Caucasus region, but the rebels, who have always said a troop withdrawal was a condition for peace, are likely to react angrily to his announcement.
Earlier on Thursday, Lebed and Maskhadov had agreed measures to build on a shaky truce and political deal aimed at ending the 21-month-old conflict.
